To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the gliadin proteins in Chinese Spring wheat are encoded by genes at the Gli loci on the homoeolocus group 6 and 1 chromosomes and 2) the tetrasomic 6D chromosome in Chinese Spring wheat lines carries deletion of a chromosome region at the Gli locus.
the gliadin proteins separated into two groups: α-gliadims encoded on the homoeolgous group 6 and γ-gliadims on the homoeoligous group 1.

the 2-DE analysis of gliadins in wheat aneuploids and the molecular characterization of the α-gliadin Glia-α 9, a CD epitope-containing protein, have provided new insights into the molecular basis of CD immunotoxic proteins in wheat and have provided a genetic resource for the reduction of immunotoxic proteins in breeding programs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular characterization of gliadin proteins of wheat and the identification of the genes responsible for the celiac disease immunotoxic epitopes.
the molecular characterization of gliadin proteins of wheat and their relationship with CD.

the molecular characterization of gliadin genes and their encoded proteins in Chinese Spring wheat, which may provide a basis for understanding the structure, function and regulation of the gliadin genes and their encoded products, and for the molecular characterization and breeding of wheat for the improvement of food quality.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 2-DE technique is a very useful tool for the characterization of wheat gliadins and for the study of gliadin gene organization.
the gliadin proteins of wheat were encoded by multigene families and their genes were distributed on the homoeolgous groups 1 and 6 chromosomes at Gli-1 and Gli-2 locus, respectively.
the α-gliadin proteins encoded on chromosomes 2A, 6A, and 6B are the major CD elicitors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the α-gliadin spots assigned to chromosome arm 1DS were absent in tetrasomic 5A lines, and the γ-gliadin spot assigned to chromosome arm D5S was absent in tetrasomics 5A lines.

2-DE is a powerful technique for the characterization of wheat gliadins and the detection of chromosome-specific gliadins, which is important for the development of wheat varieties with reduced CD toxicity.

we identified the gliadin proteins in Chinese Spring wheat, and we found that tetrasomic chromosome lines carry deletion of chromosome segment at the gliadin locus, which may provide a genetic resources for the reduction of celiac disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
2-DE can be used to characterize and quantify gliadins, which is useful in the study of wheat gluten and CD.
the wheat seed storage proteins, gliadin and glutenins, are encoded by a large multigenes.
the 2-DE method can be used to profile gliadin protein spots and to determine the chromosomal location of each spot.
